items.title: Activation contract for extension-contributed Space sidebar elements
items.summary: Specification 4763-4866 requires a Plugin's sidebar element to open an arbitrary configured page/URL, an authorised app surface, an authored CUI page or a generative page, or invoke an Automation. The stable identity model already exists (Haven.Core ExtensionSidebarContribution: SidebarItemId/Label/IconKey/TargetKind/TargetId, carried on ExtensionPackageManifest.SidebarContributions) and per-Space visibility exists as SpaceCapabilityBinding(CapabilityId = Manifest.PackageId, Kind = Plugin, Override). What is missing is the runtime contract: an IBrowseNativeAppContentSession such as the Spaces session has no host hook to navigate its own tab to an arbitrary address or to open another app surface, and no reviewed service resolves ExtensionSidebarTargetKind to an authorised target. The Home launcher opens apps through a different, Browse-host-owned path, so reusing it from Spaces would be an invented channel. Implementation has therefore landed only the authored area and stable identity projection (commit aec18695, renders nothing until a projection is supplied); no disabled placeholder rows and no fake activation were shipped. Owner decision needed: which typed host contract owns sidebar-element activation (a session-level open-address/open-app-surface callback, a shared navigation service, or an extension runtime resolver), and which target kinds are in scope for the Spaces sidebar now versus the Plugins milestones (F08/H06). Affected change held: wiring spaces.sidebarItems from the attached-extension projection in Haven.Desktop and implementing spaces.open-sidebar-item in the Spaces session.
items.resolution: Owner direction 2026-10-19: DEC-014 described an implementation gap in already-required behaviour, and routine engineering decisions are authorised under existing policy. Resolved by reusing the existing typed host navigation contract rather than creating a competing framework: BrowseNavigationIntent plus BrowseNativeWorkspace.QueueNavigation, the same path the Home launcher already uses, passed into SpacesBrowseAppContentFactory and the Spaces session as a narrow optional extension. Commits 9fc92762 and 06e7bac8. Remaining scope on the requirement, tracked as implementation work rather than a product decision: Automation and GenerativePage target kinds are not yet opened, and no native journey has been driven with a real attached extension.
